cohort: 348 newborns who were examined during their fetal life in the third trimester of pregnancy, divided into a study group with prenatally diagnosed ductal constriction and a control group without.
finding: Neonates with a prenatal diagnosis of ductal constriction are prone to transient respiratory problems (up to 27%), mild neonatal hyperbilirubinemia (up to 43%) requiring phototherapy, and longer hospitalization.
